enum: JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies
JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies

cross_tool_domains.attrition: Not directly applicable to repeated municipal administrative registries (no individual cohort follow-up), though uneven temporal completeness creates longitudinal gaps: INEGI Land Use Series II was excluded as incomplete (PDF p. 5), age-disaggregated gastrointestinal morbidity was available only for 1998 and 1999 (PDF p. 7), and years with zero recorded disease cases ("non-detected" diseases) were omitted from the non-parametric regressions rather than modeled as zeros or missing-data mechanisms (PDF p. 6).
cross_tool_domains.confounding: High concern (uncontrolled): all comparisons are purely ecological across N = 3 municipalities with no statistical adjustment, stratification, or standardization for major confounders, including substantial population growth and age-structure differences when plotting raw annual cancer death counts (Fig. 4, PDF p. 8), severe clinic/physician scarcity and diagnostic shifts over 1998–2019 (PDF p. 11), Helicobacter pylori prevalence, diet, household sanitation/hygiene, migration, and non-waterborne occupational agrochemical exposures.
cross_tool_domains.legal_measurement_quality: Adequate for descriptive legal-administrative mapping: the study operationalizes formal water-allocation rules using geo-referenced permit records from CONAGUA's Public Registry of Water Rights (REPDA, 1994–2019) disaggregated by source (groundwater, surface water, federal/sewage discharge), use category (agricultural, public urban/domestic, livestock, industrial/services), and allocated water volume (hm3), accurately situated within CONAGUA's centralized >2,500-inhabitant urban priority scheme, Mexico's 2012 Article 4 constitutional human right to water, and APARURAL (PDF pp. 5–7, 9). However, legal permits measure authorized rather than metered extraction, spatial clipping rules between watershed and municipal polygons are unspecified, and informal ejidal water governance is described only anecdotally without systematic coding (PDF p. 9).
cross_tool_domains.measurement_bias: High concern: no direct water-quality, agrochemical, or biological exposure measurements were performed; permitted water concessions proxy formal allocation rather than actual household water access or quality; gastrointestinal morbidity relies heavily on "indeterminate" infections and severe rural healthcare under-ascertainment (PDF pp. 7, 11); mortality trends attribute 838 broad ICD causes (including unspecified malignant stomach tumors) to pesticides and plot raw death counts rather than age- or population-standardized rates despite rapid demographic growth (PDF pp. 6, 8–9); and an unedited data/reporting error states that the three municipalities have "a population of 295 persons" on PDF p. 4 versus 295,698 inhabitants across the three municipalities on PDF p. 7.
cross_tool_domains.outcome_measurement_quality: Weak (high concern): formal domestic versus agricultural concession shares capture administrative allocation rather than realized household drinking-water continuity, potability, or sanitation service levels, while downstream health outcomes rely on unstandardized municipal morbidity and mortality counts subject to acknowledged clinic/doctor scarcity, diagnostic indeterminacy ("indeterminate" gastrointestinal infections and unspecified stomach tumors), and lack of denominator adjustment for population growth (PDF pp. 6–8, 11).
cross_tool_domains.reporting_bias: Some to high concern: no pre-registration or analysis protocol is reported; water-concession analysis is framed in Methods as "a qualitative, spatially explicit representation" (PDF p. 6) but reported quantitatively as concession counts, shares, and volumes (hm3) in Results and Discussion without complete municipal denominator tables or maps of the concessions themselves; gastrointestinal morbidity regression curves are summarized only in text while raw cancer death curves are plotted selectively in Fig. 4 (PDF pp. 7–8); and the exact list of 838 pesticide-associated mortality causes is omitted (PDF p. 6).
cross_tool_domains.selection_bias: High concern for inferential generalization, moderate for descriptive municipal coverage: the study purposively selects three municipalities in the RGCLM watershed (Comitán de Domínguez, La Trinitaria, La Independencia) using complete municipal administrative registries, but omits "non-detected" disease years from regression fits (PDF p. 6), restricts age-stratified morbidity analysis to 1998–1999 (PDF p. 7), uses an unpublished screening list of 838 mortality causes (PDF p. 6), and introduces unsystematic anecdotal observations from community fieldwork in the Discussion without any sampling or recruitment protocol in Methods (PDF p. 9).

domain_ratings.justification: Accurately cites the 2012 constitutional reform to Article 4 of the Constitución Política de los Estados Unidos Mexicanos establishing the human right to water and domestic priority, CONAGUA's 10-year renewable federal water-concession system recorded in the Public Registry of Water Rights (REPDA), and the rural water/sanitation program APARURAL, though statutory provisions of the Ley de Aguas Nacionales governing permitting and enforcement are summarized generally rather than cited to exact articles.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 5–6 (Methods: SDG 6), p. 9 (Discussion: Individual and collective action), p. 12 (References)

domain_ratings.justification: Clearly delineates both the biophysical boundary (the 81,000 ha endorheic karstic Río Grande de Comitán-Lagos de Montebello watershed, including the 6,000 ha Lagunas de Montebello National Park / Ramsar site bordering Guatemala) and the three principal Mexican municipal jurisdictions in Chiapas (Comitán de Domínguez, La Trinitaria, and La Independencia), alongside federal (CONAGUA), state/municipal (APARURAL), and community/ejidal governance tiers.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 4–5 (Study area; Fig. 2; Methods: SDG 15), p. 9 (Discussion: Individual and collective action)

domain_ratings.justification: Defines administrative water-rights exposure via geo-referenced CONAGUA REPDA concessions (1994–2019) categorized by water source (groundwater, surface water, federal/sewage discharge) and permitted use (agricultural, public urban, livestock, industrial/services), alongside INEGI land-cover classes (2002, 2007, 2017) and municipal Palma ratio and CONAPO Marginalization Index measures; however, legal concessions capture permitted rather than metered water extraction, and agrochemical/water-contaminant exposures are not directly measured.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 5–7 (Methods: SDG 15, SDG 6, SDG 10; Results), p. 9 (Discussion)

domain_ratings.justification: While municipal water-concession allocation shares and volumes (hm3) are intelligible administrative indicators, health outcomes rely on broad municipal morbidity groupings (dominated by poorly defined "indeterminate" gastrointestinal infections) and an unverified screening list of 838 causes of death "potentially associated with pesticides" (primarily unspecified malignant stomach tumors) plotted as raw death counts rather than population- or age-standardized mortality rates.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 6–8 (Methods: SDG 3; Results; Fig. 4), p. 9 (Discussion)

domain_ratings.justification: Clearly specifies the three watershed municipalities and draws on complete municipal-level Mexican administrative registries and censuses (INEGI, REPDA, DGEPI, SINAVE, CONAPO) over stated years, but introduces unsystematic observations from "field work and interaction with the community members" in the Discussion with zero description of sampling, locations, or participant numbers in Methods.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 4–6 (Study area; Methods), p. 9 (Discussion: Individual and collective action)

domain_ratings.justification: Justifies selecting the RGCLM watershed as a degraded karstic basin and notes exclusion of minor vegetation types and incomplete INEGI Series II cartography, but omits years with zero recorded cases ("non-detected" diseases) from local polynomial regressions, restricts age-stratified morbidity analysis to 1998–1999, and provides no reproducible inclusion/exclusion rules for the 838 pesticide-linked mortality causes.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 2, 5–7 (Introduction; Methods: SDG 15, SDG 3; Results)

domain_ratings.justification: Names official secondary data sources and software (ArcGIS 10.3), but omits critical measurement procedures: Methods describe the REPDA analysis as "a qualitative, spatially explicit representation" whereas Results and Discussion report exact concession counts and volumes (hm3) without explaining how watershed vs. municipal boundaries were reconciled; Fig. 4 plots raw annual death counts without population denominators despite rapid demographic growth; and PDF p. 4 erroneously states the three municipalities have "a population of 295 persons" while PDF p. 7 reports 166,178, 83,111, and 46,409 inhabitants (295,698 total).
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 4–9 (Study area; Methods; Results; Fig. 4; Discussion)

domain_ratings.justification: Purely descriptive ecological juxtaposition of four unlinked municipal/watershed time series across N = 3 municipalities with no comparator arm, counterfactual strategy, or exposure-outcome regression model (local polynomial fits only smooth disease/death counts over calendar time); linking unequal water concessions, land-cover change, and agrochemicals to gastrointestinal morbidity and cancer mortality suffers from severe ecological fallacy and unverified attribution, which the authors partly acknowledge as "an unresolved issue".
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 6–8 (Methods: SDG 3; Results; Fig. 4), pp. 10–11 (Discussion; Conclusion)

domain_ratings.justification: Performs no statistical control, age standardization, or population-rate adjustment for major confounders—including rapid population growth, age distribution, extreme scarcity of clinics/physicians and changing diagnostic reporting over 1998–2019, Helicobacter pylori and dietary factors in stomach cancer, household sanitation, migration, and direct occupational agrochemical handling—relying solely on narrative discussion.

Provides thorough multi-scalar institutional context linking CONAGUA's centralized permitting bias toward urban centers (>2,500 inhabitants), the 2012 constitutional human right to water, malfunctioning municipal wastewater treatment in Comitán de Domínguez vs. septic/direct river discharge in rural municipalities, federal rural programs (APARURAL, Sembrando Vida, UMAs), greenhouse-tomato land/water grabbing, and informal ejidal dry-season irrigation bans and rainwater harvesting.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 7, 9–11 (Results; Discussion: Individual and collective action, Economy and finance, Governance)

domain_ratings.justification: While INEGI, CONAGUA REPDA, DGEPI, and CONAPO datasets are public Mexican administrative sources, weekly municipal morbidity data required an unpublished official request (Official Letter No. DGE-DGAE-01350), no code or processed datasets are archived, the exact 838 ICD mortality codes derived from toxicology textbooks are unreported, and GIS spatial filtering rules for REPDA concessions are unspecified.

Summarizes high-level groupings for INEGI land cover (7 classes), REPDA water concessions (source and use categories), and gastrointestinal morbidity (4 groups), but provides no explicit crosswalk or validation for the 838 pesticide-associated mortality codes, no rules for distinguishing missing surveillance years from zero-count years, and no coding protocol for informal community governance observations.

Contains no researcher positionality, reflexivity, or fieldwork ethics statement, despite invoking unsystematic field observations and interactions with local community members in the Discussion and proposing governance and financial interventions for marginalized rural and indigenous populations.

raw_response.overall_narrative_summary: Rodríguez-Izquierdo et al. (2023) present an illustrative ecological-institutional watershed case study of three municipalities in the Río Grande de Comitán-Lagos de Montebello (RGCLM) karstic basin in Chiapas, Mexico (Comitán de Domínguez, La Trinitaria, and La Independencia), examining interlinkages among land-cover change (SDG 15), formal water concessions (SDG 6), gastrointestinal morbidity and pesticide-suspect mortality (SDG 3), and socioeconomic inequality (SDG 10), alongside governance levers (SDGs 11, 12, 16). Appraised under the 13-domain Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework (structured non-validated judgment), the study demonstrates strong jurisdictional specificity and institutional contextualization—effectively documenting how CONAGUA's centralized federal water-concession system (REPDA, 1994–2019) concentrates 90% of permitted domestic public water volume in urban Comitán de Domínguez while allocating 88% of agricultural water volume to rural La Trinitaria and La Independencia despite Mexico's 2012 constitutional human right to water (Art. 4). However, methodological rigor for empirical health and causal inference is weak: the four secondary municipal datasets cover misaligned periods across N = 3 municipalities with no statistical exposure-outcome model or comparator; pesticide and water-contaminant exposures are unmeasured; non-parametric time-trend fits omit zero-record disease years and plot raw cancer death counts rather than age- or population-standardized rates despite rapid population growth; 838 mortality causes are attributed to pesticides without publishing the ICD code list; community fieldwork observations appear in the Discussion without any qualitative methods in the Methods section; and minor internal reporting errors occur (e.g., reporting total population as "295 persons" on p. 4 versus 295,698 inhabitants across the three municipalities on p. 7).
raw_response.overall_rating: High methodological concern for causal health inference; adequate descriptive legal-institutional mapping (structured non-validated judgment)
raw_response.study_design_identified: Descriptive ecological-institutional watershed case study combining four multi-period municipal administrative/GIS datasets (land cover 2002–2017, REPDA legal water concessions 1994–2019, municipal morbidity/mortality time trends 1998–2019, and census/marginalization indices 2000–2020 across N = 3 municipalities) with institutional governance analysis
raw_response.where_found_summary: Abstract (PDF p. 1); Introduction & Conceptual approach (PDF pp. 1–4); Study area & Methods across SDGs 15, 6, 3, and 10 (PDF pp. 4–6); Results & Figs. 3–4 (PDF pp. 7–9); Discussion of Individual and collective action, Economy and finance, and Governance (PDF pp. 9–11); Conclusion & Declarations (PDF pp. 11–12).
raw_response.why_tool_chosen: Independent inspection of the Methods section (PDF pp. 4–6) shows that this study fits none of the six conventional epidemiological, qualitative, or review designs in RISK_OF_BIAS.md §1: it is not a randomized trial (RoB 2), not a non-randomized intervention evaluation with a comparator arm (ROBINS-I), not an individual-level cohort study (JBI Cohort), not a cross-sectional survey or analytical exposure-outcome regression (JBI Analytical Cross-Sectional—datasets span separate multi-decade windows across N = 3 municipalities and the only regressions are univariate local polynomial smoothers of disease/death counts against calendar year), not a primary qualitative or mixed-methods study with documented qualitative data collection/analysis in Methods (ruling out CASP and MMAT despite passing mention of field observation in the Discussion), and not a systematic review (AMSTAR 2). Instead, it is an empirical-institutional case study integrating administrative legal water-rights registry data (CONAGUA REPDA concessions), cartographic/vital-statistics series, and doctrinal/institutional governance analysis (Article 4 Mexican constitutional water rights, CONAGUA permitting, APARURAL, and ejidal water rules), for which the 13-domain Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework (RISK_OF_BIAS.md §2) is the exact matching instrument.
